kind: T2 video/audio ground-truth times and video<->logger offsets (Fuji 2020-07-29/30)

labels.measured: computed directly from the local video/audio/XRK by the scripts in this folder
labels.estimated: depends on an assumption stated next to it

signConvention:
lag / offset L > 0 means the logger (IMU / GPS) feature occurs L seconds LATER than
the video/audio feature when the video is placed on the lap clock with the overlay-timer mapping
(video-timer-reads.json). Equivalently: true lap t of a video frame = overlay-mapped lap t + L.

timeBases.lapT: shipped lap JSON t (0 = first GPS sample of the lap), GPS time base = viewer clock
timeBases.imu: XRK 50 Hz, t = (logger_ms - tc0)/1000 + shift (shift = lap meta channel_time_alignment on 7/30, 0 on 7/29)
timeBases.pts: ffmpeg PTS of SCHD0613/0624.MOV; both files start mid-GOP: the first decodable frame has PTS 1.000 s

audioStreams.verdict: stream index 1 is the cabin microphone (band energies follow speed/RPM; engine orders and kerb rumble visible). Stream index 2 is not sound: constant level identical on both days, ~1 % full-scale samples, no correlation with speed or RPM; it is a binary data track (see datatrack_summary.json).

dataTrackCalibration.label: measured on 7/30 (6 laps)
dataTrackCalibration.definition: transientYawLag - dtLoggerClock (s): true lap t of a frame = data-track logger-clock lap t + this

videoYawSignals.farScene: median horizontal Farneback flow of textured far-scene pixels (rows < 200 px, mostly the right windshield area); forward-motion parallax not removed
videoYawSignals.groundPlane: shared intercept A of u = A + k_row*(x - 640) fitted (IRLS) over textured ground-band pixels (rows 200-292 px) on both sides of the FOE column; ground parallax removed

explanation.label: derived from the measured numbers above
explanation.summary: The 0.185-0.285 s 'video yaw lead' is a real time offset between the scene in the video and the overlay LAP timer used to place the video on the lap clock: the scene is about 0.198-0.211 s later on the lap clock than the overlay timer says (7/30 measured 0.135-0.274 s per lap, median 0.211; 7/29 estimated 0.171-0.234, median 0.198). It is not vehicle physics and not a GPS processing delay.
evidence: Video yaw is the rigid-body yaw of the camera, the same motion as the gyro; the transient (0.5-3 Hz) lag of the gyro behind the overlay-mapped video yaw is 0.135-0.274 s per lap on 7/30 (mean of two independent video estimators, which agree within 0.04 s on every lap).

Kerb strikes are physically simultaneous in sound, camera shake and accelerometers: the cabin-audio rumble onsets lead the accelerometer onsets by a median 0.23 s (15 high-confidence 7/30 events, overlay map); after applying each lap's yaw-derived offset the residual is 0.013 s (median, IQR +-0.05 s): audio and video yaw agree on the offset.

The gyro agrees with the GPS position course rate within +-0.025 s on 7/30 and -0.015..-0.041 s on 7/29 (gyroVsGpsCourseRateLagS), so the old comparisons against GPS course rate saw the same ~0.2 s; accy/v adds a few hundredths of physical lag (lateral acceleration builds after yaw rate), which is why that reference gave larger numbers.

The SmartyCam data track (audio stream 2) stores, for every 5th frame, the logger clock and the newest GPS epoch held by the camera. On 7/30 the scene's true lap time equals the data-track logger-clock lap time -0.054 +- 0.01 s (6 laps), and the newest GPS epoch is about 0.12 s older than the scene. The overlay-timer lap time is 0.01-0.13 s older than even that GPS epoch, i.e. the overlay graphics are rendered from a data snapshot about 0.2 s older than the image (the pedal bars a further ~0.09 s older).
The lap-to-lap spread of the overlay-based offset (0.135-0.274 s) is reproduced by the data track to +-0.01 s, so it comes from the 3 manual overlay-timer reads per lap, not from the clocks.

Clock rates from the data track: GPS iTOW vs video PTS -8.7 / +19 ppm (7/29 / 7/30); logger clock vs PTS -101 / -104 ppm. The logger clock therefore drifts ~0.11 ms/s against GPS, which is the growth of the 7/30 per-lap shift (0.497 -> 0.583 s); on 7/29 the same drift (~40 ms over laps 1-4) is not corrected in the shipped data (shift 0).
residualUnknowns: The ~0.05 s by which the camera-held logger time leads the scene is either camera capture-to-record latency or IMU filter delay; the data cannot separate them (estimated).

7/29 offsets are estimated: the wet video yaw is too noisy at 0.5-3 Hz (rain, fog, wipers), so the 7/30 data-track calibration is applied assuming the same camera/logger latency; one high-confidence 7/29 kerb event agrees within 0.02 s.

ECU_STEER_ANG turn-in onsets are not earlier than the gyro onsets (median +0.03 s right-hand, +0.14 s left-hand corners on 7/30), although steering must precede yaw: the ECU steering channel likely carries extra latency (estimated) and should not be used as a sub-0.1 s time reference without calibration.
Video turn-in onsets per corner have estimator-dependent left/right biases of about +-0.1 s; use the lap offsets, not single corners, for clock work.

answers.howToUse: For a video frame at PTS p in lap k: true lap t = p - lapStartPtsCorrected[k] - delta[k] (= overlay-mapped lap t + bestOffsetS[k]). Equivalent data-track form (7/30, measured): lap t = (loggerMs(p) - libxrkOffsetMs - tc0Ms)/1000 + shift + (-0.054) s.
